title: Reducing and reusing cardboard packaging
subtitle: From delivery boxes to packing material, how to extract full value before recycling
excerpt: Single-use cardboard from online deliveries is one of the most visible and rapidly growing household waste streams. Flattening and recycling is the minimum; using boxes for storage, garden mulching, craft, and moving saves the energy and water needed to recycle the card. Recycling is third in the hierarchy, behind reduction and reuse.
sourceNotes: WRAP (Waste and Resources Action Programme): paper and cardboard recycling data, lifecycle analysis of cardboard versus virgin fibre. Recycle Now UK guidance on cardboard recycling preparation. Paper Industry Technical Association (PITA) on fibre quality and recycling limits.

glossaryTerms.definition: Cardboard with a fluted inner layer sandwiched between two flat liners, giving high strength-to-weight ratio. The most common material for delivery boxes. Can be recycled 5 to 7 times before the fibres become too short.

content.text: runs: avoid, reduce, reuse, then recycle. Most households go straight to recycling. Recycling is better than landfill, but reuse is better still.

Garage and loft storage: decant the box contents, fold the box flat for storage, or reuse structurally for other stored items. A clean, undamaged delivery box stores well for 2 to 3 years in dry conditions.
Garden mulching: lay flat sheets of cardboard around plants as weed suppression (see cardboard mulching entry). Remove all tape and staples first; tape does not decompose and blocks worm movement.

Compost feedstock: torn into pieces no larger than A4, cardboard is an excellent 'brown' carbon source for a compost heap. The corrugated structure aerates the heap as it decomposes. Ink on cardboard is now predominantly soy-based and is not a compost contaminant.
Packing for shipments or resale: a clean box in good condition replaces the need to buy packaging.
Children's crafts and seedling pots: kitchen roll tubes and produce trays both make free biodegradable seedling containers.
Remove all packing tape. Tape is made from polypropylene film and is not recyclable; it contaminates cardboard bales.
Flatten boxes completely to maximise bin capacity. Flattened boxes take up one fifth the volume of whole boxes in the recycling bin.
Remove any polystyrene inserts, ice packs, or plastic liners before placing in the recycling bin.

Do not compost or recycle waxed cardboard (pizza boxes with heavy grease saturation, wax-coated produce boxes). Grease-contaminated cardboard degrades paper fibre quality in the recycling process. Lightly marked pizza boxes are usually still accepted for recycling; heavily soaked boxes are not.
Combine online orders into fewer, larger deliveries. Each delivery generates a box, no matter how small the item.
Buy in bulk where unit cost and shelf life allow: a single large box has a lower packaging-to-product ratio than multiple small boxes.

rows.symptom: Cardboard left in the recycling bin has got wet and turned to pulp
rows.cause: Cardboard in an open or unsealed recycling bin absorbs water and loses its fibre structure, making it harder to process
rows.fix: Keep cardboard dry until collection day. If the bin is exposed to weather, store cardboard inside and add it on collection morning. Some local authorities specify that wet cardboard is not accepted; check your council's guidance.
